findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the runaway error escapes the three maps' existing catch-all `except Exception: ... break` fail-open wrappers (acli_graph.py :245/:347/:440) — e.g. re-raise the named error outside the fail-open, or narrow the handler — so a stalled cursor propagates loudly instead of becoming a silent partial map (cabc AC#3).
evidence: acli_graph.py :245 `except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 — fail-open: degrade gracefully` then `break` (repeated at :347, :440)
cited bug rebar:cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c AC: 'the fail-open except Exception no longer converts a stalled cursor into a silently partial whole-project map'
cabc description: 'each reader wraps the POST in a fail-open except Exception ... the error is then swallowed at WARNING — so the pass completes with a SILENTLY PARTIAL map'
findings.finding: The three maps each wrap their cursor loop in a catch-all `except Exception: ... break` fail-open handler (acli_graph.py :245-251, :347-353, :440-446). A RunawayPaginationError raised by the new shared iterator INSIDE that try block would be swallowed and converted into a silently-partial map — the exact cabc failure mode — so the guard would not actually surface, and the strict-xfail (which asserts the reader stops within two requests, not a swallowed spin) would not flip green. The plan does not enumerate editing these fail-open handlers.
findings.location: Approach / Scope (acli_graph.py 'three loops -> shared cursor iterator + runaway guard')
scenarios: Server repeats the same nextPageToken; iterator raises RunawayPaginationError; the surrounding `except Exception` catches it and returns a partial map instead of propagating.
The strict-xfail test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own still fails because the reader returns a partial dict rather than stopping loudly within two requests.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the shared iterator's runaway error either be raised outside the per-request try/except, or be explicitly re-raised before the `except Exception` catch-all (e.g. `except RunawayPaginationError: raise`), and add a test asserting the map does NOT return a partial dict on a repeated token.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the runaway error escapes each map's fail-open `except Exception` (e.g. re-raise RunawayPaginationError from the handler, or drive the iterator so the guard raises OUTSIDE the try) so a stalled cursor is loud rather than swallowed into a partial map (cabc AC3).
evidence: acli_graph.py:245-251 / :347-353 / :440-446 — each map wraps the POST in `except Exception as exc: ... break` returning the accumulated partial map
cabc AC3: 'the fail-open except Exception no longer converts a stalled cursor into a silently partial whole-project map'
cabc mechanism note: 'the spin ends only when the transport itself finally errors, and that error is then swallowed at WARNING — so the pass completes with a SILENTLY PARTIAL map'
The held-out oracle test asserts the reader stops on its own within two requests AND does not rely on the harness hard-stop — a swallowed raise would still fail that oracle
findings.finding: The plan's loud RunawayPaginationError can be swallowed by each map's existing fail-open `except Exception: ... break`, reproducing the silent-partial-map symptom the plan aims to eliminate. The plan does not specify that the runaway error must escape the fail-open handler.
findings.location: Approach section ('raises a loud RunawayPaginationError when the server returns the same non-null token twice')
scenarios: Server repeats the same non-null nextPageToken with isLast falsy; iterator raises inside a next() call that is pulled within the map's try block; `except Exception` catches it and returns the partial map instead of propagating
findings.suggested_fix: State that the shared iterator's runaway error is a distinct type re-raised past (or raised outside) the fail-open handler, and add a test asserting a repeated token propagates the error rather than returning a partial dict.
